# Widget manufacturing notes

A widget is a stamped steel bracket used to join two lengths of conduit. The design has not changed
much since the 1960s, mostly because the conduit standard has not changed either.

Three grades exist. Grade A is galvanised and rated for outdoor use. Grade B is untreated and
cheaper by about 40 percent. Grade C is a thinner gauge that most inspectors will reject, though it
still sells in volume for temporary structures.

Cost per unit at our volume runs to 0.34 in steel and 0.11 in labour. Freight adds another 0.06 if
the order ships under a pallet load, which is where small orders lose money.

The failure mode worth knowing about is galvanic corrosion where a Grade B bracket touches copper.
It takes about two years in a damp environment. We stopped selling Grade B for indoor plumbing work
after a warranty claim in 2019.
